page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a compute-oriented virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 x86_64 processor. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, along with 32 GB of system memory, providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache resources consist of 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 variants such as VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, SHA_NI, and FMA. This instance features dedicated CPU allocation, includes no attached local storage, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-core processing capabilities, positioning its single-thread stress-ng throughput in the top quartile of tested instances. Multi-core compute performance, Geekbench scores, PassMark CPU ratings, and web serving throughput of 10.45 GB/sec fall within average bounds. However, memory subsystem tests indicate lower uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 37.36 GB/sec read and 14.86 GB/sec write for 256MB blocks. Additionally, medium LLM inference tasks show limited throughput, making the instance less suitable for memory-bandwidth-intensive AI execution.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides solid compute density for general-purpose application hosting and single-thread intensive tasks without paying for specialized acceleration or built-in NVMe storage. It is well-aligned with web serving, software compilation, database key-value operations such as Redis, and general CI/CD pipeline execution.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a compute-focused instance powered by a 4-core AMD EPYC 9B14 processor providing 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Featuring advanced instruction support including AVX-512, AES, and SHA_NI, it lacks local storage and GPU hardware. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top quartile, alongside average multi-core execution, PassMark CPU, and static web serving capabilities reaching 10.45 GB/sec. A notable hardware tradeoff is lower uncached large-block memory bandwidth, which constrains performance in memory-bound applications like medium-scale LLM inference. Financially efficient as a balanced compute node without bundled storage costs, c3d-standard-8 is best suited for general web serving, Redis key-value workloads, software compilation, and standard application hosting.
